key_insight: Physics-constrained causal discovery can identify constitutive mechanisms from full-field displacements, but separating correlated environmental effects requires interventions.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports constitutive models that generalize across climates and guides informative experiments without measuring stresses or internal variables.
method: Embed balance laws and constitutive skeletons in time-unrolled causal graphs scored by weak-form equilibrium gaps.
Use adaptive lasso and a NOTEARS-type acyclicity constraint to select mechanism dependencies.
Compute a Gauss–Newton identifiability certificate via automatic differentiation to guide greedy D-optimal test design.
evidence_signal: In a synthetic plate study with 0.01-pixel displacement noise, interventional data recovered the exact 8-edge graph in 7 of 10 runs and kept climate-transfer errors within 3.2%, versus up to 41.5% for observationally discovered models.
watch_item: Evidence is synthetic, and weak-form score noise bias remains a primary limitation.
paper_title: Physics-constrained differentiable causal discovery of constitutive mechanisms through boundary value problems
